newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open lower.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open lower.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open lower Monday, in line with LME copper prices, after a further rise in LME stocks.

COMEX September copper was seen opening down 0.50 to 1.00 cent a pound from Friday's close at 100.00 cents, after sliding last week to six month lows as supply continued to outweigh demand during the slow summer season.
LME warehouse copper stocks jumped another 3,725 tonnes Monday to 264,600 tonnes, with stocks now at their highest level since last September.
COMEX copper stocks rose 1,308 short tons Friday to 37,889 short tons.

Metal continues to flow into LME warehouses in Europe reflecting the summer shutdowns in that part of the world, while in the U.S. over 3,000 tonnes arrived in exchange warehouses in Baltimore late last week.

Weakness in South East Asian economies is seen lowering demand in Asia also, with Japanese exports of copper falling to 71,030 tonnes in the first half of 1997, from 88,160 tonnes. Japan's copper exports go mainly to China, Taiwan, Thailand and South Korea.
